public_rationale: The forecast rests on a premise Marcus himself labels presumptive: Google was not already earning sufficiently large AI returns. The reviewed disclosures do not establish that premise. Later records show substantial AI revenue and continued expansion, but do not provide matching AI-only costs and net returns. The conditional forecast therefore cannot be scored. Its open-ended timing also means that continued investment through the evaluation date is not failure.
limitations: This is not a finding that the forecast is false.
A revenue-based reading of zillions would materially change the assessment.
The proposed returns-or-termination test interprets an unspecified form of eventual adjustment.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Google is presumably not already making zillions from AI (or it would have said so on the investor call), and that situation cannot continue indefinitely.

statement.excerpt: If they were already making zillions from AI, they would have mentioned that on the investor call. But presumably they are not, and that cannot continue indefinitely.

from_speaker: If they were already making zillions from AI
they would have mentioned that on the investor call
our_interpretation: Zillions is colloquial for very large financial returns, not a numerical quantity.
The surrounding discussion of making back investment makes adequate returns after costs the relevant reading, rather than revenue alone.
The forecast rests on the unverified premise that Google's AI investment was not already producing such returns at the time of the post.
The predicted change is eventual adequate returns or an end to the investment effort that fails to produce them.
No deadline or numerical threshold is added. The claim's baseline premise must be established before a later event can be scored.
criteria.support_condition: First establish inadequate AI financial returns at the baseline; then document either substantial returns relative to costs or termination of the uneconomic investment effort.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Continued investment without established adequate returns for any finite period does not contradict an indefinite forecast. Evidence that the baseline premise was false would make the conditional forecast inapplicable.

evidence.locator: Anat Ashkenazi's prepared remarks, Google Cloud results
evidence.explanation: Enterprise AI was generating substantial quarterly revenue. The disclosure does not establish net returns after all attributable costs or verify the forecast's baseline premise.

The surrounding remarks attribute Cloud growth largely to AI demand and describe continued capacity expansion. They establish neither an end to the effort nor AI-only net returns sufficient to meet the early-resolution rule.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Establish the baseline premise and define the return measure and accounting basis; then obtain a matching financial disclosure or a documented termination of the uneconomic investment effort.
